A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations and experiments on MPI3D-Complex and Causal3DIdent, including semantic recovery, downstream prediction, and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the experimental appendices.

M1.justification: The latent-variable model, selection and perturbation mechanisms, MMCL objectives, and encoder architectures are retained. Rewritten explanations and notation corrections do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same numerical simulations, MPI3D-Complex, and Causal3DIdent, covering independent/dependent semantics, semantic recovery, and ID/OOD downstream prediction. Added dataset illustrations introduce no new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The same linear, logistic-regression, and nonlinear MLP probes participate in the corresponding comparisons. No competing evaluated method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the fixed selection during perturbation tests from I_theta = [9] to [10] and specifies that the OOD transformation acts on latent semantic coordinates. Both settings were already described this way in v1 Appendix D.1; these are reported-setting corrections without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: The encoding-dimension ablations, combined selection/perturbation experiment, linearity analyses, OOD tests, and text-representation analyses are retained in the corresponding renumbered appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds/runs and retain the same averaging and uncertainty displays. The plotted uncertainty bands match after accounting for changed axis scales.

E6.justification: Corresponding heatmap values, numerical results in Tables 4–5, downstream curves, and ablation results match. Changes to plot colors, scales, and numbering do not alter the reported findings.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, both corollaries, the two lemmas, and the proof arguments are retained. Explicit reminders of inherited assumptions and uniformity, plus the expanded indexing example, explain existing mathematics without adding a substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that MMCL identifies unbiased shared semantics and that misalignment can impair semantic coverage or support invariant representation learning. The revised title and abstract preserve these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of semantic exclusion, latent dependence, discretization, and excess encoding capacity are retained. The limitations concerning fixed selection biases, random missingness, and guarantees beyond nonlinear identifiability also remain.

D1.justification: Architectures, optimization settings, sample splits, text templates, hardware, runtimes, and code-access information were already documented in v1 and remain available in v4. Rewriting, relocation, and notation corrections add no substantive reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v4 adds Schölkopf et al., Toward Causal Representation Learning (2021), removes the Tversky–Kahneman Judgment under Uncertainty reference, and refines discussion of ICA assumptions and invariant mechanisms. The four principal related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction, experimental setup descriptions, and portions of the appendices. The title and terminology change, and related work moves from v1 Appendix B into v4 Section 6, substantially reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: Figures are systematically reformatted with revised palettes, fonts, legends, markers, and standardized downstream axis ranges. The model diagram and MPI3D examples move, a Causal3DIdent sample strip is added, and appendix plots and tables are regrouped.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity and consistency by correcting the simulation setup, tightening explanations, bringing related work and dataset examples into the main text, and making plots easier to compare. The theory, empirical evidence, and limitations remain stable, so the overall gain is limited to explaining and presenting the existing work more effectively.
